scenario: Class 12 student from a school or college seminar with no course selected
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, good to have you at the {{event_topic}} session at {{college_name}}. Most students your year are stuck on the same thing, which qualification to start with and when. We have a short assessment that maps your subjects and interests to a finance path. Should I send it here?
notes: Never open with a course name for this cohort

scenario: Class 12 student from organic Instagram asking whether CFA is possible after Class 12
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, short answer: CFA registration needs you to be in the final year of a bachelors degree or have work experience, so it is not a Class 12 entry point. What people in your position usually do is start with a graduation plan that runs alongside it. Want the eligibility sheet plus the two routes that are actually open right now?
notes: Correct the premise plainly then offer the real route. Verify current CFA Institute entry rules before send

scenario: Parent enquiring about ACCA for a child after Class 12
message_text: Good morning. You had asked about ACCA for {{student_name_if_parent}}. Three things usually decide it: how it runs alongside graduation, what the total cost across all levels comes to, and where students land after. I have put all three in one guide. Should I send it, or would you rather we talk it through on a call this evening?
notes: Answer outcome and cost before anything else. No slang. No urgency language

scenario: College first year student who downloaded a career guide
message_text: Here is the Finance Career Roadmap you asked for. One thing worth knowing in first year: the sequencing matters more than the course. Some qualifications are best started now and some are wasted if you start too early. Which of these is closer to you right now: exploring options, or already fairly sure about finance?
notes: Resource first then the question. Never reverse the order

scenario: College second year student interested in CFA
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, you were looking at CFA Level 1. In second year the useful question is timing. Register too early and you burn an attempt, too late and it misses placements. It depends on your graduation year and how many hours a week you actually have. Which graduation year are you?
notes: Timing is the real question for this cohort not the syllabus

scenario: Final year student interested in job oriented finance skills
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, you had mentioned placements when we met at {{college_name}}. The honest gap for most final year students is not knowledge, it is that they cannot show work. Recruiters screen on a model you have built, not a course you have enrolled in. We have a short skills check that shows exactly where you stand. Want it here?
notes: Do not name a course until a role is named

scenario: Final year student interested in Analyst Stack
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, Analyst Stack is built around what an analyst actually does in the first year of the job, so the fit depends on the role you are aiming at. Equity research, investment banking and corporate finance each need a different emphasis. Which one are you targeting?
notes: Role first. The product only makes sense against a role

scenario: Graduate comparing CFA with an MBA
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, CFA against MBA is really two different bets: depth in one domain versus a network plus a general management route. The right answer depends on whether you already have a finance role you want to go deeper in, or you are trying to change track entirely. Which of the two is your situation?
notes: Never argue for CFA. Diagnose the situation

scenario: Job seeker interested in Financial Modelling
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, you asked about the Financial Modelling program. Since you are in the middle of applications, the useful thing is knowing which model type comes up in your target interviews. It is different for banking, equity research and corporate finance. Which roles are you applying to right now?
notes: Speed matters. Send within 5 minutes of lead creation

scenario: Working professional asking about CFA Level 1
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, on CFA Level 1 with a full time job, the two things that decide it are the attempt you pick and the hours you can actually give in a week. We have batch variants built for both ends of that. How many hours a week are realistic for you: under 8, 8 to 15, or 15 plus?
notes: Tappable ranges. Never ask an open ended hours question

scenario: Working risk professional asking about FRM Part 1
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, since you are already working in {{current_role}}, FRM Part 1 will overlap with a fair amount of what you do daily and the new load sits mostly in quant and valuation. Worth seeing how it is taught before you commit. Want the sample session on the quantitative portion?
notes: Domain overlap is the honest and most persuasive framing

scenario: Working professional asking only for fees
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, fee depends on the variant, so both numbers: Full Immersion is {{fee_full_immersion}} and the Accelerate track is {{fee_accelerate}}, both inclusive of taxes. The difference is live hours versus self paced. Which of the two are we deciding between?
notes: Answer with numbers. Never deflect a fee question to a call. Fee variables must come from the live fee master

message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, sending the sample session now. It is a full concept from the actual course, not a trailer, so watch fifteen minutes and you will know whether the depth works for you. I will check back after you have seen it.
notes: Never send a highlight reel to a professional evaluating teaching

trigger: course enquiry after a faculty video
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, since you are already through CA material, a lot of Level 1 will be revision for you and the genuinely new part is ethics, portfolio management and the quant treatment. There is a batch built specifically for CA and MBA finance students that moves faster through the overlap. Want the coverage and hours for that one?
notes: Real SKU on the SSEI course page. Use it

message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, Level 2 opens the moment your result is out and the gap between levels is where most people lose time. Level 2 is heavier on application than recall, so the study pattern that worked at Level 1 usually needs changing. Want the Level 2 plan mapped to the next window?
notes: Owner is student success. Cross sell not acquisition tone

message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, for the next window the only thing worth doing first is finding out which topics actually cost you the marks, because a repeat of the same study plan usually gives the same result. We have a twenty question diagnostic that gives you a topic level view. Want it?
notes: Never open with the failure. Never use sympathy language

message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, most FRM Part 1 repeats come down to two or three topics rather than the whole paper, usually quant and valuation. Worth confirming that before you plan the next attempt. Should I send the topic diagnostic?
notes: Same principle as CFA retakers. Diagnose then offer

scenario: ACCA student enquiring about a single paper
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, we do run paper level packages, so you are not forced into a full level. Which paper is it, and is this your first attempt at it or a repeat? The plan differs quite a bit between the two.
notes: Two questions maximum and both are necessary here

scenario: Existing SSEI student eligible for cross sell
trigger: course completion at 60 percent or above
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, you are past the halfway mark on Level 1, well done. One thing that comes up at this point: the charter proves you know the theory, interviews still ask you to build. Analyst Stack is the practical half of that. Want a two minute look at what it covers before you decide anything?
notes: Never pitch to a student who is behind schedule or has an open ticket

scenario: Meta advertisement lead with no response after the first message
trigger: no reply for 48 hours after first message
message_text: {{first_name}}, easier if I just ask directly. Which of these are you: still deciding what to do after graduation, or already preparing for a specific exam? One word is enough and I will send only what is relevant.
notes: Switch from open question to binary choice. Never write just following up

scenario: Google Search lead for a specific course
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, on FRM Part 1 the two things people usually want first are the next batch start and whether the quant load is manageable alongside work. Next batch starts {{batch_start_date}}. Which of those two matters more to you right now?
notes: Search leads arrive with a question. Answer it in line one

scenario: Organic YouTube viewer enquiring after a faculty video
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, glad the session on {{event_topic}} was useful. That topic sits inside {{course_name}}, and the full treatment runs a fair bit deeper than a video allows. Are you studying this for an exam, or watching to decide whether the subject is for you?
notes: Never send a faculty introduction video to someone who arrived from one

message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, thanks for staying through the {{event_topic}} session. The question that came up most in the chat was how to choose between the certification route and the skills route. It genuinely depends on your graduation timeline. Which year do you finish?
notes: Continue the session. Never restart the conversation from zero

trigger: event ended and attendance is no_show
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, you had registered for {{event_topic}} and could not make it. Here is the recording. The part most people replay is the section on which qualification suits which career stage, around the twenty minute mark.
notes: Deliver the promise before anything else. No sales content in this message

message_text: Hi, this is {{counsellor_name}} from SSEI. Someone shared our CFA guide with you and you opened it, so a quick check before I send anything else. Are you looking at CFA for yourself, and if so are you a student or working? Reply STOP any time and I will not message again.
notes: This person never opted in. Consent language is mandatory. Requires legal review

scenario: Referral lead from a current student
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, {{referrer_name}} passed on your number and said you are looking at CFA. They started at roughly the same point you are at now. Before I send anything, are you planning the {{next_attempt_window}} attempt or still deciding on the timing?
notes: Confirm the referrer agreed to be named before using the name

message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, {{counsellor_name}} here, following up on our call. As discussed: {{call_summary_line}}. Sending the two things you asked for, the batch calendar and the fee by variant. Anything else you want before we fix the attempt?
notes: Summarise the call in the lead words. Never send a generic template after a call

scenario: Walk in lead at an offline centre
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, good meeting you at the {{centre_name}} centre today. As we discussed, the {{batch_name}} batch starts {{batch_start_date}} and there are {{seats_remaining}} seats in that slot. Do you want me to hold one while you confirm?
notes: Only mention seat counts when the number is genuinely accurate

scenario: Tier 2 city lead preferring offline learning with no centre nearby
trigger: mode preference offline and offline_accessible false
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, you had mentioned classroom learning. Being straight with you: our classrooms are in {{centre_list}} and {{city}} is not one of them. What we do have is the same faculty teaching live online with doubt sessions, which is what most students outside those cities use. Want a three minute look at how that class actually runs?
notes: Address the preference honestly. Never pretend the centre exists

scenario: Tier 3 city lead requiring online guidance
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, everything we run is available online with live classes and recordings, so location is not the constraint. The real constraint is usually deciding what to aim at. Two options so I send the right thing: career direction first, or a specific exam you already have in mind?
notes: City tier changes logistics wording only. It must never change tone or priority

message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, before I send anything on CFA, one thing so I get the right version to you. Are you currently studying or working? The batch and the plan are genuinely different for the two.
notes: One question. Give the reason for asking it

message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, so I do not send you the wrong thing, which is closer to where you are: you want a finance qualification but are not sure which one, or you want practical skills for placements? Either is fine, they just lead to very different starting points.
notes: Two clear options. Never send a list of all courses

scenario: Lead who requests a payment link immediately
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, happy to send it. One confirmation first so the link is for the right thing: {{course_variant}} for the {{attempt_window}} attempt at {{fee_amount}}. Confirm and the link comes in the next message.
notes: Never send a link before the variant and price are confirmed. Never add education content here

message_text: {{first_name}}, the payment did not go through, the amount will come back to your account if it was debited. Usually it is a card limit or the bank OTP timing out. Here is a fresh link, and if it fails again tell me and I will send a UPI or bank transfer option instead.
notes: Lead with reassurance about the money. Counsellor task at P0 in parallel

scenario: Lead who says the course is too expensive
message_text: Understood. Two honest things: there is a lower priced variant that covers the same syllabus with fewer live hours, and there is a three part instalment option on the main program. Which of those is closer to what would make it workable for you?
notes: Never open with a discount. Never say it is an investment

scenario: Lead who says they need time
message_text: That is fair. So I am not chasing you for no reason: when would you want to actually start, around {{option_a}} or closer to {{option_b}}? I will set a reminder for then and leave you alone until it.
notes: Convert a delay into a dated re entry. This single rule cuts follow up fatigue more than any other

scenario: Lead comparing SSEI with another provider
message_text: Fair question, and you should compare. The difference people usually point to with us is depth of teaching rather than speed, and the honest way to judge that is a full session rather than my opinion. Sending one now. If you want a straight comparison after that, {{counsellor_name}} will give it to you without the sales pitch.
notes: Never disparage a competitor in writing. Let the class do the arguing

scenario: Lead who is not eligible for the requested course
message_text: {{first_name}}, being straight with you: {{course_name}} needs {{eligibility_requirement}}, so it is not open to you yet. What is open right now is {{alternative_course}}, and students usually do that first and move across later. Want the two year sequence written out?
notes: State the reason plainly. Always name the open route. Never sell around the rule

message_text: Done, you will not get any more messages from us. If you ever want to pick this up again just message here and we will start from wherever you left off.
notes: Single confirmation message only. Then full suppression across every channel

trigger: new batch or new fact available
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, we spoke back in {{last_contact_month}} when the timing was not right for you. One thing has changed since: {{new_fact}}. If it is still on your mind, say so and I will send the details. If not, tell me and I will close the file properly.
stop_condition: Reply received or 2 attempts across 90 days
notes: A new fact is mandatory. Give an explicit exit. It protects the list

scenario: School cohort follow up after no reply to the assessment offer
message_text: {{first_name}}, simpler version of the same question. Which of these three sounds most like you: CA, CFA and ACCA all sound the same to me, or I know I want finance but not which exam, or I already know what I want. Any one of them is fine.
notes: Open question failed so switch to fixed choices

scenario: School cohort follow up after an eligibility correction
message_text: {{first_name}}, one thing I should have added. Students who want CFA eventually usually pick a graduation subject that carries over into it, which saves close to a year later. Want the one page on how to sequence it?
notes: New value in every follow up. Never repeat the previous ask

scenario: Parent follow up after no reply
message_text: Following up on ACCA for {{student_name_if_parent}}. The three questions parents ask most are total cost across levels, whether it runs alongside graduation, and what happens after. Happy to answer all three on a call, or in writing here if that is easier. Which do you prefer?
notes: Parents prefer conversation. Offer both and let them choose

scenario: First year student follow up after the roadmap was opened
trigger: resource opened and no reply at 72 hours
message_text: {{first_name}}, you had a look at the roadmap. The one decision that matters in first year is whether you start a qualification alongside college or build skills first. Which way are you leaning?
notes: Question must reference the resource they actually opened

scenario: Second year follow up after no reply
message_text: {{first_name}}, just the graduation year is enough and I will tell you the attempt that fits. It takes ten seconds and saves you registering a year too early, which is the most common and most expensive mistake here.
notes: Reduce the ask to one word

scenario: Final year follow up after the skills check offer
message_text: {{first_name}}, one number from the last placement season: most students who cleared finance interviews had built two or three models before the interview, not after. The skills check tells you which ones you are missing. Two minutes, want it?
notes: Use only claims that can be evidenced. Verify this statistic before use

scenario: Analyst Stack follow up when no role was named
message_text: {{first_name}}, pick whichever is closest and I will send the version that matches: equity research, investment banking, corporate finance, or not sure yet. Not sure yet is a perfectly good answer.
notes: Make the uncertain option explicitly acceptable

scenario: Comparison follow up for a graduate
message_text: {{first_name}}, one line that usually settles it: CFA is the better bet if you want to go deeper into a finance role you can already get, an MBA is the better bet if you need to change track and build a network. Which of those two is your problem?
notes: Give the actual answer. Do not hoard the insight for a call

message_text: {{first_name}}, if you are mid applications the fastest thing you can add to a CV in four weeks is a built model you can talk through in an interview. Want to see what the first two weeks of the program cover?
notes: Speak to the live pressure which is the interview

scenario: Professional follow up when hours were not answered
message_text: {{first_name}}, pick a number and I will tell you which variant is realistic: under 8 hours a week, 8 to 15, or 15 plus. If it is under 8 I will tell you honestly whether the attempt you want is doable.
notes: Willingness to say no is what makes the yes credible

scenario: FRM follow up after no reply
message_text: {{first_name}}, sending the quant session anyway since that is the part people want to test first. Fifteen minutes will tell you whether the pace works alongside your job.
notes: Remove the friction and just send the asset

message_text: {{first_name}}, if the number is the issue rather than the course, say so directly and I will show you the instalment split and the lower priced variant. No pitch involved.
notes: A silent lead after a fee quote is usually a price problem. Name it

trigger: no reply at 48 hours after the class was sent
message_text: {{first_name}}, did you get a chance to watch any of it? Even a straight it was too fast or too slow is useful, it changes which batch I would put you in.
notes: Invite the negative answer. It gets replies and it is genuinely useful

message_text: {{first_name}}, quick estimate for you: with CA behind you roughly {{overlap_pct}} of Level 1 is revision. Which attempt are you thinking about, so I can tell you whether that timeline is realistic?
notes: Overlap percentage must come from an approved academic estimate not from the message writer

message_text: {{first_name}}, no pressure on deciding now. Just one thing worth knowing: registration for {{next_window}} closes {{deadline_date}} and starting after that compresses the whole plan. Want me to send the dates?
notes: Deadline must be a real published date. Never invent urgency

scenario: Retaker follow up after the diagnostic offer
message_text: {{first_name}}, if the diagnostic feels like too much right now, just tell me the two topics you found hardest last time and I will send you the specific sessions on those. That is the actual starting point.
notes: Lower the effort. Retakers avoid anything that resembles another test

message_text: {{first_name}}, just the paper code is enough and I will send the coverage, the hours and what it costs on its own.
notes: Single word reply required

message_text: {{first_name}}, leaving this here for after your exam. Students usually add the practical piece once the theory is done, and there is a combined price if it is bought alongside your current course. Nothing needed now.
notes: Respect exam season. Explicitly remove the pressure

scenario: Meta lead second no response attempt
message_text: {{first_name}}, last message from me on this. If finance is still something you are thinking about, reply anything and I will pick it up. If not, no problem at all and I will close it here.
stop_condition: No reply means state moves to dormant
notes: Give a clean exit. It improves both list health and reply rate

message_text: {{first_name}}, studying for an exam or just exploring the subject? Either answer is fine, it only changes what I send next.
notes: Explicitly permit the low intent answer

message_text: {{first_name}}, sending the comparison sheet from the session anyway, the CA versus CFA versus ACCA one people asked about. Have a look and tell me which route you are leaning towards.
notes: Deliver the thing the audience asked for during the session

trigger: no reply at 72 hours after the recording
message_text: {{first_name}}, if the recording is still unopened it is probably not the right time, which is fine. Next session is on {{next_event_topic}} on {{next_event_date}} if that is closer to what you needed.
stop_condition: Reply received or 2 attempts then dormant
notes: Accept the signal. Do not push the same asset a third time

message_text: No reply needed if this is not relevant, and I will not message again after this one. If CFA is something you are looking at, just say student or working and I will send the right version.
notes: Never send more than two messages to someone who did not opt in

message_text: {{first_name}}, {{referrer_name}} mentioned you were thinking about the {{next_attempt_window}} attempt. Is that roughly right, or is the timing still open? Either way I will send what matches.
notes: Use the referrer context. It is the strongest asset in this journey

message_text: {{first_name}}, on the point you raised about {{objection_summary}}, here is the direct answer: {{objection_answer}}. If that settles it, the next step is only picking the attempt.
notes: Answer the specific objection raised on the call

message_text: {{first_name}}, holding the seat until {{hold_expiry}} and then it opens up again. If something is holding you back tell me what it is and I will deal with it directly.
notes: Only state a hold expiry that is genuinely enforced

message_text: {{first_name}}, one option if classroom is genuinely important to you: the {{nearest_centre}} face to face batch, with the travel that involves. Worth comparing against the live online one before you rule either out. Want both details side by side?
notes: Present the real trade off rather than pushing online

message_text: {{first_name}}, easier question. Are you in your final year of college or already done? That alone decides what I should be sending you.
notes: Life stage is the highest value single field to recover

message_text: {{first_name}}, studying or working? One word and I will send the CFA plan built for that situation rather than a generic one.
notes: Repeat the ask once with the reason attached

message_text: {{first_name}}, if it helps, here is the short version. Qualification route is slower and opens more doors long term. Skills route is faster and helps immediately at placements. Which problem are you solving right now?
notes: Give real information in the follow up rather than another request

message_text: {{first_name}}, holding the link until you confirm the variant. Reply 1 for {{variant_a}} or 2 for {{variant_b}} and it goes out immediately.
notes: Reduce the confirmation to a single digit

trigger: no completion at 2 hours after the retry link
message_text: {{first_name}}, still not through. Two alternatives that usually work: UPI directly, or a bank transfer with the receipt sent here. Which do you want to use? {{counsellor_name}} can also do it over a call in five minutes.
notes: Change the payment method rather than resending the same link

message_text: {{first_name}}, no pressure at all. If the timing of the money is the issue rather than the amount, the instalment split moves most of it to later. Say the word and I will send exactly how it breaks up.
notes: Separate the amount problem from the timing problem

message_text: {{first_name}}, you had said {{agreed_month}} was when you wanted to look at this properly. That is now. Batch for {{attempt_window}} starts {{batch_start_date}}. Still on?
notes: Quoting their own words back is the single highest response rate follow up in this library

message_text: {{first_name}}, whichever way you go, one thing worth checking on any provider: ask for a full class rather than a demo edit, and ask how doubts are handled after the class. That is where the real difference shows.
notes: Useful advice that is true regardless of choice builds more trust than a claim

message_text: {{first_name}}, sending the two year sequence anyway so you have it. The short version is that what you pick for graduation decides how smooth the CFA route is later.
stop_condition: Reply received or 2 attempts then nurture
notes: Stay useful even when there is nothing to sell today

message_text: {{first_name}}, going quiet on this now. When board results are out and you are deciding on graduation, message here and I will help you plan it. No messages from me until then.
stop_condition: Move to dormant with a dated re entry at the results window
notes: A dated re entry beats an indefinite nurture list

message_text: Leaving this here. Whenever you want to discuss {{student_name_if_parent}} plans, message on this number and we will pick it up. Nothing further from us until then.
notes: Parents respond badly to persistence. Two attempts maximum

message_text: {{first_name}}, leaving you to it. When you are in second year and thinking about internships, that is the right time for this conversation. I will check in then if that is alright.
stop_condition: Dormant with a dated re entry at the second year window
notes: Set the return date explicitly

message_text: {{first_name}}, pausing here. If the CFA question comes back when placements start, this number works. I will send one note when the next attempt registration opens and nothing else.
stop_condition: Dormant with one dated event trigger
notes: One future trigger only. State it so it is not a surprise

message_text: {{first_name}}, stopping here so I am not adding to the noise during placements. If you want the skills check or a call at any point, message this number.
notes: Placement season is the wrong time for volume. Say so

message_text: {{first_name}}, closing this off. If the CFA versus MBA question comes back, the comparison sheet is still here whenever you want it.
notes: Leave the door open without a further ask

message_text: {{first_name}}, all the best with the applications. If an interview asks for something you have not built yet, message here and we will fix that quickly.
stop_condition: Dormant with a 60 day reactivation eligibility
notes: Genuinely useful exit line for this cohort

trigger: no reply at 48 hours with intent score above 60
message_text: {{first_name}}, you were fairly close to deciding and then it went quiet, which usually means one of three things: the fee, the timing, or something at work. Which one is it? I will deal with whichever it is directly.
stop_condition: Counsellor call task at P1 immediately
notes: A previously hot lead going silent is a blocker not a content gap. Name the three likely blockers

trigger: no reply at 24 hours after a fee quote
message_text: {{first_name}}, {{counsellor_name}} will call you at {{proposed_time}} unless you tell me otherwise. Five minutes, only to sort out whatever is pending.
notes: State the time. Never say someone will call soon

trigger: resource completion above 50 percent and no reply at 72 hours
message_text: {{first_name}}, you watched most of it so the teaching is clearly not the issue. Is it the fee, the timing, or the attempt you are unsure about?
notes: Use the behavioural evidence you actually have

message_text: {{first_name}}, pausing this. Most CA students look at CFA seriously right after their final result, so I will check in around {{result_month}} unless you get there sooner.
stop_condition: Dormant with a dated re entry at the result window
notes: Anchor the re entry to a real calendar event

message_text: {{first_name}}, leaving it here. If you decide to go for {{next_window}}, message me and we will build the plan around the topics that actually need work.
stop_condition: Dormant with a dated re entry at the registration window
notes: No sympathy language even at exit

message_text: {{first_name}}, closing this for now. When you fix the paper and the sitting, message here and I will send the package for exactly that.
notes: Short and functional for a transactional cohort

message_text: {{first_name}}, no more messages from me. The sessions stay up on the channel, and if it becomes an exam thing rather than an interest thing, this number works.
notes: Respect the low intent signal

message_text: {{first_name}}, stopping here. You will get an invite when the next session is on a topic worth your time, nothing else.
stop_condition: Dormant with event invite eligibility retained
notes: Event invitations are the least intrusive reactivation channel

message_text: {{first_name}}, leaving this. If you want to talk it through, {{referrer_name}} knows how the course runs and can tell you honestly. This number also works whenever.
notes: Hand the relationship back to the person the lead actually trusts

trigger: no reply at 24 hours after the call follow up
message_text: Counsellor call script. Open with the exact question the lead asked on the first call. Confirm the variant and attempt. Ask directly what is pending. Close on either a payment link or a dated decision.
notes: This is a call task not a message. Recorded and audited

message_text: Counsellor call script. Reference the centre visit and the specific batch discussed. Ask what changed since the visit. Offer either the seat or a dated follow up. Do not re pitch the course.
notes: Walk ins are the highest intent leads in the system

message_text: Counsellor call script. Establish whether the classroom preference is about discipline or about doubt clearing. If discipline offer the live batch with attendance tracking. If doubts offer the doubt session structure.
notes: Mode preference is usually a proxy for a different concern

message_text: No further automated contact. Monthly counsellor sweep only if fit_score is at 60 or above.
notes: Low intent plus no reply does not justify counsellor time

message_text: Counsellor call script. One call to establish studying or working and target attempt. If unreachable in two attempts move to dormant.
notes: One human attempt is worth more than five automated messages here

message_text: Move to dormant. Retargeting audience eligible if consent permits. No further one to one messaging.
notes: Paid social leads with no reply belong in an audience not in a counsellor queue

message_text: Counsellor call script. Confirm variant and price verbally. Issue the link on the call and stay on the line until the payment page loads.
notes: Staying on the line through checkout is the single biggest recovery lever

trigger: two failures or no completion at 24 hours
message_text: Counsellor call script. Confirm no double debit. Establish the failure reason from the gateway code. Offer UPI or bank transfer. Escalate to finance if the debit is unresolved.
stop_condition: Counsellor call task at P0 plus finance ticket
notes: Money anxiety must be resolved before any sales conversation resumes

message_text: Counsellor call script. Establish whether the constraint is total amount or cash flow timing. Offer the lower variant or the instalment split. Do not offer a discount without approval.
notes: Discount authority sits with the sales manager and must be logged

trigger: no reply at 72 hours after the dated re entry
message_text: Counsellor call script. Reference the date the lead chose. Ask whether the plan changed. Close on enrolment or a final dated decision.
notes: Two dated re entries maximum then dormant

message_text: Counsellor call script. Ask what specifically they are comparing on. Use the internal comparison brief. Never disparage. Offer a full class or a faculty conversation.
notes: Competitor leads are time sensitive. Call within one working day

scenario: Postgraduate student evaluating a qualification alongside a masters
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, since you are already doing {{current_qualification}}, the useful question is what CFA adds that your programme does not. In practice it is the depth on valuation and portfolio work plus the credential recruiters recognise globally. Want the coverage list so you can see the overlap yourself?
notes: Marginal value is the only argument that works here. Never explain what CFA is

scenario: Senior finance specialist checking coverage in a niche
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, given what you already do, most of the value is likely in two or three specific areas rather than the full program. Which topics are you actually checking coverage on? If it is a narrow set, partial topics may be the better route and I will say so.
notes: Never pitch the full program before checking whether partial topics fit

scenario: FRM Part 1 student progressing to Part 2
message_text: Hi {{first_name}}, Part 2 opens once your Part 1 result is out, and it leans much harder on application and cases than Part 1 did. Most people who leave a gap between the two lose the momentum. Want the Part 2 plan mapped to the {{next_window}} sitting?
notes: Owner is student success. Mirrors the CFA progression pattern
